properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the usage ledger names a caller only from the initialize handshake. A stateless call (MCP 2026-07-28) has none, and rmcp fills it with its own library name and version, so the hook's graph probe reads as a harness called `rmcp 3.3.0`. Even a stateless caller that declares itself in `_meta` is recorded as `rmcp`
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (the hxm_program hub's first /feedback report, 2026-09-14, reflow2 0.60.2) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "Two clients appear: `claude-code 2.1.270` (29 calls) and `rmcp 3.3.0` (20). The second is not this session and I cannot attribute it; the project runs hooks at session start and stop, which is the likely source." EXPECTED: every caller named as what it is; req:feedback-on-reflow2-is-computed-from-a-record-the-server-kept asks for "which agentic platform". NOT AFFECTED: callers that do an initialize handshake are named correctly (claude-code, reflow2-mcp --call, smoke_mcp).

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): the same client was seen twice on 2026-09-12 and never walked. fact:the-first-real-usage-report-classed-four-of-five-refusals-as-other saw 22 of 113 calls as `rmcp 3.3.0` and guessed "a proxy that re-initialises after a daemon respawn declares rmcp's default client info". fact:loop-status-cost-is-amplifiers-not-baseline-and-80pc-of-calls-are-automation saw 32 of 39 loop_status calls from `rmcp` and named the Stop-hook path in tools/loop_nudge.py "the leading candidate, unverified".

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) PROXY RESPAWN: the stdio proxy re-initialises a respawned daemon with rmcp's default client info (the 09-12 guess).
(B) HOOK PROBE: the hook's graph probe (tools/graph_probe.py, spawned by loop_nudge.py) calls the shared server statelessly, with no handshake, and the server supplies a default name.
(C) A REFLOW2 CLIENT: some reflow2 code acts as an rmcp client with a default ClientInfo.
(D) CONTRACT: the ledger's naming was written for a transport where every call has a handshake. The capability says "the harness name and version from the handshake". A stateless request's own `_meta` clientInfo is never read.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: a real harness or another person's session named itself `rmcp`.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM:
· A predicts rmcp lines across every tool, and only after a daemon respawn.
· B predicts rmcp lines only on the tools the probe asks (loop_status, unclaimed_findings).
· C predicts an rmcp client in the 0.60.2 source.
· D predicts a stateless call that DOES declare its clientInfo is still recorded as rmcp.
· E predicts varied tools.

⑤ RESULTS:
· REFLOW2'S OWN LEDGER (5,096 calls, 2026-09-12 to 09-28): 465 calls from `rmcp`, 170 at 3.3.0 and 295 at 3.4.0. Those are the rmcp crate versions of the 0.60.2 and 0.74.0 builds (Cargo.lock at each tag). EVERY ONE is loop_status (272) or unclaimed_findings (193), exactly the two tools graph_probe.call asks. ⇒ B HOLDS; A and E REFUTED.
· CODE, the proxy: since 2026-07-27 (280397c), proxy.rs keeps the client's own initialize (`hello`) and replays it VERBATIM to a respawned daemon. ⇒ A REFUTED in code as well.
· CODE, clients: at v0.60.2 no reflow2 code acted as an MCP client. `--call` arrived 2026-09-19 (#544) and names itself "reflow2-mcp --call". ⇒ C REFUTED.
· CODE, the probe: graph_probe.call puts protocolVersion and clientCapabilities in `_meta`, and NO clientInfo.
· CODE, the library: rmcp 3.4.0 (streamable_http_server/tower.rs, peer_info_for_stateless_request) builds `client_info: Implementation::default()`, the library's own name and version, and ignores the request's `_meta`.
· CODE, the server: service.rs call_tool reads the caller from `peer.peer_info()` only. Its `unknown` branch is unreachable for a stateless call.
· SCRATCH STORE, 0.74.0 `--http`, first call: a stateless tools/call made exactly as graph_probe makes it was logged `client: rmcp, client_version: 3.4.0`.
· SCRATCH STORE, second call: a stateless call that DECLARED `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"] = {name: graph-probe, version: 1}` was ALSO logged `rmcp 3.4.0`. That is the key SEP-2575 provides, and rmcp's RequestMetaObject::client_info reads it. ⇒ D HOLDS.
⇒ CAUSE, AT TWO LAYERS. The only stateless caller reflow2 ships, the hook's probe, declares nothing. And the server names every call from the handshake alone. So a stateless call carries the MCP library's name as if it were a harness, whether or not it declared itself.

⑥ CLASS: a value the transport did not carry is filled by a library default and recorded as data. This is the BL-198 class: a default nobody chose reads as a fact. The same `client` variable feeds content_policy::for_client, so a stateless client that declares itself (grok, opencode) would be served the content shape chosen for `rmcp`. That consequence is INFERRED FROM CODE, not measured. Would a fix at the class have stopped the earlier report? Yes: the 22 rmcp lines of 2026-09-12 are the same probe.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE; no code was changed. A test pinning the class would assert four things:
· a stateless tools/call carrying `_meta` clientInfo is recorded under the declared name;
· one carrying none is recorded as undeclared (for example `stateless, undeclared`), never as the MCP library's own name;
· the content policy resolves from the same identity;
· graph_probe declares itself, so the hook's calls read as automation in every tally.
Today the wire test (tools/test_feedback_is_a_computed_tally.py) pins naming only for an initialize-based client.

PROPOSED FIX: this answers the report's own question, "whether hooks' calls should be labelled as such", so it is recorded here rather than as a new idea.
· When the handshake carried no client, read the per-request `_meta` clientInfo.
· Name an undeclared stateless caller as undeclared.
· Have the probe declare itself.
The feedback skill could then say which rows are automation.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS:
· HELD: the second client was not the session, and it was hook-driven.
· QUALIFIED: it is not "the hooks" as such but the stateless probe they spawn. A hook that shells out through `--call` is named correctly.
· OVERTURNED: the 2026-09-12 guess recorded in fact:the-first-real-usage-report-classed-four-of-five-refusals-as-other (proxy re-initialisation after a respawn).
· VERIFIED: the 2026-09-12 "leading candidate, unverified" in fact:loop-status-cost-is-amplifiers-not-baseline-and-80pc-of-calls-are-automation, through graph_probe.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
· The hxm work machine's own ledger was not read. The checkout on the maintainer's machine is a second-machine copy begun 2026-09-23, with no rmcp lines. That its 20 rmcp calls were the probe is inferred from the reflow2 ledger's 465-of-465 match and the shared kit.
· The content-policy consequence is inferred from code.
· Whether the same-second duplicate probe pairs noted on 2026-09-12 come from two hook events firing together was not measured.
